summary.headline: Atlanta Electricals Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 48% YoY to INR466.33 crore; record order inflow of INR972.42 crore lifted order book to INR3,116.63 crore.
summary.overview: Revenue grew 48% YoY to INR466.33 crore, driven mainly by volume from newly commissioned plants, with management saying pricing and product mix were broadly unchanged. Gross margin rose 130 bps to 27.3% and EBITDA margin expanded to 16.5% from 15.5% a year ago, though both moderated from Q4 FY26 seasonally. Order inflow was a record INR972.42 crore, taking the unexecuted order book to about INR3,117 crore, of which about INR2,400 crore is expected to execute in FY27. Management reiterated a 40% revenue CAGR target and a 17-18% margin range, while 400 kV and 765 kV product timelines were pushed out and largely remain conditional.

segments.name: Product mix by voltage class
segments.commentary: 220 kV class was 56% of Q1 revenue, 66 kV class 25%, and 132 kV class about 5.5%. Power transformers were about 79% of revenue, with auto, inverter duty and other products making up the balance.

segments.name: End market
segments.commentary: Transmission and distribution contributed about 66% of revenue and renewable energy about 19%, with thermal power and other industrial making up the rest.

segments.name: Order book by voltage
segments.commentary: 220 kV and above transformers are over 55% of the order book; 400 kV transformers and reactors account for nearly INR275 crore. Management said the entire record Q1 inflow is 220 kV and below.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue target of 40% YoY growth, applied to FY26 revenue of INR1,851 crore (per CFO); management also cited a 40% CAGR for three years.
EBITDA margin expected around 17-18% for the year, with raw material inflation expected to persist but margins sustainable at the Q1 level.
About INR2,400 crore of the ~INR3,100 crore unexecuted order book is due for execution in FY27.
Inverter duty transformer facility (~5,000 MVA) targeted for commissioning by end-December 2026.
Export target of about 15% of revenue within three years; no export revenue in Q1 FY27 and first export execution expected in FY28.
Management expects meaningful revenue from 400 kV transformers from FY28, with 765 kV tech tie-up targeted by end-Q2 FY27 and first 765 kV product by Q4 FY27.
capex_capacity: Installed manufacturing capacity of 63,060 MVA; Q1 sales-based utilisation of 4,381 MVA, of which Vadod produced 1,520 MVA and Ankhi (Jambusar) 320 MVA.
Inverter duty transformer facility adds ~5,000 MVA; construction on track for commissioning by end-December 2026.
Vadod Unit 4 received Power Grid approval for 400 kV class manufacturing; first 400 kV unit under engineering completion, with short-circuit test planned around quarter-end (Q1 FY27 end or early Q2).
Tank and radiator backward-integration facility adjacent to Vadod: INR15-20 crore spent so far against about INR180 crore planned; tanks and radiators are 4-5% of transformer cost.
765 kV plan: first product to be made at Ankhi once technical tie-up closes; Power Grid revalidation needed in new name. Short-circuit test requirement for 765 kV not yet finalised.
demand_pricing: Record order inflow of INR972.42 crore in Q1 FY27; order book INR3,116.63 crore as of 30 June 2026.
Key orders: INR291.68 crore from RVPNL (160 MVA, 50 MVA, 31.5 MVA power transformers) and INR285.15 crore from PSTCL (23 units of 160 MVA 220/66 kV transformers).
Pricing passed through via price variation clauses in purchase orders; per-MVA realisation described as unchanged across kV classes, with raw material inflation passed on.
Management saw no pricing or bidding-intensity impact from Chinese manufacturers being allowed into PSU tenders; none had participated yet.
No data-centre orders in current order book. Management expects order booking to peak in Q2 and mid-Q3 FY27.
Management said CRGO steel prices and supply are not under pressure in the short term; DGTR anti-dumping verdict expected by end-March 2027.

qa_highlights.question: Will the new 400 kV capacity pressure incremental margins or order inflow?
qa_highlights.answer: Niral Patel said Q1 was the highest order inflow in at least 2-2.5 years, with no visible pricing correction in the market.

qa_highlights.question: Are inventory builds speculative ahead of raw material volatility?
qa_highlights.answer: Anand Sharma said procurement is strictly job-to-job with no speculation on commodity prices; inventory build is for the next quarter's executions.

qa_highlights.question: What are the 765 kV tech tie-up terms?
qa_highlights.answer: Niral Patel said the deal combines a one-time fee of USD3-5 million and royalty of 2-4% for at least three to four years, on 765 kV products only; the partner is not named.

qa_highlights.question: Can margins be sustained at 17-18%?
qa_highlights.answer: Mehul Mehta said FY25 and FY26 margins ended at 15.56% and 18.52%, and that 17-18% is the expected range, with raw material price increases continuing.

qa_highlights.question: What is the margin differential for 400 kV and 765 kV?
qa_highlights.answer: Anand Sharma said these products should earn better margins than 220 kV or 132 kV, but the exact differential will only be known after first prototypes and commercial production.

qa_highlights.question: How much FY27 revenue is implied?
qa_highlights.answer: Mehul Mehta said a 40% YoY increase on FY26 revenue of INR1,851 crore is the guidance.

risks_watch: Execution timing on 400 kV: short-circuit test for the first 400 kV unit slipped from June-July to around quarter-end; balance order quantity depends on passing it.
765 kV entry depends on closing the technical tie-up (targeted Q2 FY27), government approvals on the partner side, Power Grid revalidation and an unresolved short-circuit test requirement.

Capacity additions by peers (including mention of CG Power and Transformer Rectifiers, about 60,000 MVA in the next 3-4 months per an analyst) could pressure pricing; management expects margin protection through 400/765 kV and exports.
Raw material cost pressure from geopolitics and CRGO steel anti-dumping investigation; Q1 gross margin fell QoQ.
Working capital: inventory days at 105 and inventory build in Q1; monitor cash conversion cycle (~83 days).
Export revenue is zero so far; the 15% export target is three years out.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand and order inflow, with a strong emphasis on structural growth. Noticeably cautious and evasive on specifics: declined to name the technical partner, to quantify 400/765 kV margins, or to comment on competitors and large pending orders.
key_quotes: We have had a record order inflow and order book during quarter one of ‘27.

We believe it is not a cyclical upturn but a multi-year investment cycle supported by expansion in transmission network, renewable energy integration, battery energy storage systems and industrial electrification, railway electrification and rapid growth of data centers.
We are in the business of manufacturing transformers and not speculating on the raw material price.
So we expect the margin somewhere around 17 to 18% as we always convey to our investors.
